newsitem.title: DUBAI: Senior U.S. official hopeful on talks with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Senior U.S. official hopeful on talks with Iran.

text.p: A senior U.S. official said on Thursday he was hopeful the United States would begin dialogue with Iran within the next four years if U.S. President Bill Clinton is re-elected in November.

Assistant Secretary of State Robert Pelletreau, in the United Arab Emirates on a two-day official visit, said that while the United States opposed some of Iran's policies, the current lack of bilateral talks was unsatisfactory.
"We are open to dialogue with the government of Iran," Pelletreau told a gathering of business executives in Dubai.

"I am hopeful that when we enter the longer phase...we will be able to make a match in trying out that dialogue," he said. "Because in Washington these days there are two phases: the short term and the second term."
"Nobody thinks this is a perfect situation," he said, referring to Washington's current cool relations with Tehran.
The United States broke diplomatic ties with Iran in 1980 during a crisis over the seizure of the U.S. embassy in Tehran by Moslem militants who held 52 Americans hostage for 444 days.

The United States imposed a trade and investment ban on Iran in June 1995, accusing it of sponsoring terrorism and seeking to develop nuclear weapons. Iran denies the charges and says the United States is bent on destroying its Islamic government.
A U.S. law in effect since August tightened the sanctions.
Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati on Wednesday said Iran had no favourite in the U.S. presidential race.

"Both parties have demonstrated their stance towards...Iran over the years. Therefore, it makes no difference to Iran whichever party wins in the elections," Velayati was quoted as saying by the Iranian news agency IRNA.
